transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Yeah, I mean… the main thing that made me come in is my eating got really messed up. Like, I used to track everything pretty carefully—calories, macros, all that, kind of a project manager brain thing, spreadsheets for everything—but lately I just stopped caring.

I’d go days without real meals, just coffee and protein bars, because it felt easier and I kept thinking I’d eat later. Then I noticed my clothes were kind of hanging off me, like my belt didn’t sit right, and somehow I hadn’t even registered it before. It’s weird because normally I’m pretty on top of that stuff.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or have you lost interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy?

Yeah… yeah, I have. It kind of hit after the sponsor questioned my judgment at work. I know that sounds like a normal work thing, like people ask questions all the time, and usually I’d just make a slide or write a clean email and move on.

But this time it was like the bottom dropped out. I went back to my apartment and just sat there feeling… hollow, I guess. Really ashamed. I was crying over emails I normally would’ve handled without even thinking. And then I’d get distracted rereading them, like the wording mattered more than it did, but mostly I just felt awful.
How long have you been feeling this way? Has it been more than two weeks, or did it start more recently?

It’s definitely been more than two weeks. I think… about three months now? It started after that whole project crisis, or at least that’s when I noticed it getting bad.

I kept thinking it was just a rough week, then another rough week, and you know how work gets—there’s always some new deliverable or someone changing the deck at the last second—but the hollow feeling and the shame just kind of stayed. It didn’t really lift.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends?

Yeah… I mean, I haven’t really wanted to do any of the stuff that normally keeps me steady. Hiking, for example—I used to be the guy who’d plan the route and check the weather and pack like three extra things “just in case,” you know? Lately I just look at my boots by the door and… nothing.

Same with editing photos. I have all these folders sitting there, and normally I can lose hours in that in a good way, but I don’t even open them. I haven’t been logging meals either, which is weird for me, and there’s this woodworking project in the garage that I keep walking past. I bought the wood for it and everything, and now I just… don’t touch it. It’s strange because those things usually ground me.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or feeling restless and unable to sit still?

I’m not sure. I haven’t really clocked that specifically, like whether I’m physically slower or pacing around.

I mean, I do sit on the couch longer than I mean to, but then I’ll also get up because I remembered something dumb like the recycling or whether I left a mug in the sink, and then I lose track of why I stood up. But I don’t know if that’s “restless” exactly. I haven’t noticed people saying I’m moving weird or anything.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite, like eating a lot less or losing weight without trying?

Yeah… that’s actually part of why I came in. My eating got really messed up. I used to track meals pretty carefully—like, probably too carefully, honestly, I had this whole app setup and I’d get annoyed if the barcode scanner didn’t work—but lately I just stopped caring.

I’d go whole days without a real meal, just coffee and protein bars because they were there, or because making food felt like too many steps. And then I noticed my clothes were kind of hanging off me… like my belt needed a different notch, and I hadn’t even been trying to lose weight. It sort of snuck up on me.
Have you noticed a change in your energy levels or felt unusually fatigued, even when you haven’t been doing much physically?

I don’t really know how to separate that from just… not doing much, if that makes sense. Like, if I’m sitting around and not hiking or not working on things, am I tired, or am I just not starting?

I did notice I’ll think, “Okay, get up and make something,” and then it feels like this whole production, but then I start thinking about the kitchen layout and how my old apartment had better counter space, which is stupid because that was years ago. So… I guess I haven’t really measured my energy. I’m not sure if it’s fatigue exactly.
Even when you’re not doing much, do you find yourself feeling physically drained or lacking energy, like even small tasks take more effort than they should?

I don’t know… “physically drained” is hard for me to pin down. Like, I’ll look at the laundry and it feels like there are twelve decisions inside it, but that might be more me overthinking it than being tired.

Small tasks do feel bigger sometimes, but then I’ll also spend forty minutes reorganizing browser tabs or looking up a replacement part for something I don’t even need fixed right now, so it’s not like I’m just… flat-out exhausted all the time. I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed it as a body tired thing exactly.
Have you noticed yourself speaking more slowly than usual, or having trouble with your thoughts feeling slowed down or stuck?

I’m not sure. I mean, I’ve always kind of talked in loops, so it’s hard to tell if it’s slower or just… me trying to explain things.

Thoughts getting stuck—maybe? But not like a computer freezing, more like I start answering and then there’s this side hallway in my head. Like you asked that and I immediately thought about presentations at work, because people used to tell me I talked too fast on project calls, and then I’d make these little agendas with timestamps, which honestly never worked because nobody reads them anyway.

So… I don’t know if I’m slower. I haven’t really noticed my speech being slow. My thoughts feel messy sometimes, but I don’t know if “slowed down” is the right word.
Have you experienced a time in the past few months when you completely lost interest in everything—like nothing gave you pleasure or motivation at all?

Yeah… I think so. Not like I sat down and made a list called “things I don’t care about,” but I noticed I haven’t wanted to hike, or edit photos, or even do the meal logging thing I used to be weirdly consistent about.

And there’s this woodworking project in the garage—half-finished, just sitting there—and usually that kind of thing keeps me grounded. Like sanding something down, measuring twice, all that. I used to like the order of it. Lately I don’t even want to touch it. Then I start thinking maybe the garage lighting is bad, or I need a better clamp, but… no, I think it’s more that I just don’t feel interested in any of it.
Have you experienced any significant weight loss recently, or has your appetite decreased to the point where eating feels like a chore or something you have to force yourself to do?

Yeah… that’s actually kind of one of the reasons I came in. My eating just went completely sideways. I used to track meals—like, not perfectly, but I had a system—and then I just stopped caring.

I’d go a whole day and realize I hadn’t had a real meal, just coffee and maybe a protein bar, which is ridiculous because I bought those bars in bulk after reading this whole thing about macros, and then I got obsessed with whether the chocolate ones melt in the car… sorry, that’s not the point.

The point is, yeah, eating started feeling like something I had to remember to do, not something I wanted. And then my clothes started fitting loose, like hanging off me more, and I hadn’t even really noticed until then.
Have you found yourself feeling excessively guilty about things, or like you’re not good enough, even when others might not see it that way?

Yeah. I mean… yes, definitely.

After the sponsor questioned my judgment, it was like the bottom just dropped out. And I know, logically, people question decisions all the time at work — that’s part of project management, that’s literally why we have review meetings and escalation paths and all that stuff — but I couldn’t take it like a normal comment.

I went home and just sat in my apartment feeling hollow and ashamed. Like I’d exposed something rotten about myself, not just made a questionable call. I kept opening emails I normally would’ve answered, and I was crying over them, which felt ridiculous, because they were just emails. But I felt like I wasn’t good enough to handle any of it.
Have you noticed your thoughts feeling slowed down, like it's harder to process things or make decisions, even simple ones?

I don’t know… I’m not sure I’d describe it as slowed down exactly.

Like, decisions have been harder, but sometimes that’s because I get stuck on stupid details — like if I’m trying to pick what to eat, I’ll start thinking about whether I should use what’s in the fridge before it goes bad, and then I remember I meant to clean one of the shelves, and then I’m standing there with the door open too long, which is terrible for the compressor… my dad used to get on me about that.

But slowed down? I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed it that way. It’s more like I’m scattered or just not… I don’t know, not landing on things easily.
